scenes.tts: Does a window close on its own, like a clock? Or does experience help close it?
scenes.visual: Title card: Who Closes the Window? A clock face beside a singing adult bird, with a question mark between them.
scenes.narration: Does a window close on its own, like a clock? Or does experience help close it?

scenes.tts: A young male zebra finch memorizes his tutor, usually his father, between about day twenty-five and sixty-five.
scenes.caption: A young male zebra finch memorizes his tutor, usually his father, between about day 25 and 65.
scenes.visual: A zebra finch timeline in days after hatching. A band labelled memorize spans about 25 to 65 days.
scenes.narration: A young male zebra finch memorizes his tutor, usually his father, between about day 25 and 65.

scenes.tts: He settles on a fixed, or crystallized, song by about three months.
scenes.visual: The timeline extends: a band labelled crystallized song begins at about 90 days.
scenes.narration: He settles on a fixed, or crystallized, song by about three months.

scenes.tts: Now take two groups. One hears its father sing. The other is raised without adult males.
scenes.visual: Row 1: socially reared, hears his father sing. Row 2: reared without adult males, hears no male song.
scenes.narration: Now take two groups. One hears its father sing. The other is raised without adult males.

scenes.tts: Both get a new tutor at the same late age. By then, normally reared males have stopped copying new song.
scenes.visual: Both rows fill the third column: yes, a new tutor at the same late age. A note: past the age when normally reared males stop copying. The last column shows two question marks.
scenes.narration: Both get a new tutor at the same late age. By then, normally reared males have stopped copying new song.

scenes.tts: Predict. Which group copies the new tutor? What would a clock set by age predict?
scenes.visual: The last column pulses with its two question marks. A clock icon hovers over both rows.
scenes.narration: Predict. Which group copies the new tutor? What would a clock set by age predict?

scenes.tts: A clock predicts neither copies. But Lucy Eales reported that only the birds raised without adult males copied.
scenes.visual: Row 1 fills: no. Row 2 fills: yes. The clock icon is crossed out.
scenes.narration: A clock predicts neither copies. But Lucy Eales reported that only the birds raised without adult males copied.

scenes.tts: That was in nineteen eighty-five. Later studies gave mixed results.
scenes.caption: That was in 1985. Later studies gave mixed results.
scenes.visual: Credit card: Lucy Eales, 1985. Banner: same age, different history, different outcome.
scenes.narration: That was in 1985. Later studies gave mixed results.

scenes.tts: Same age, different history. So age alone may not set the window. Hearing a tutor seems to help close it.
scenes.visual: Card: hearing a tutor helps close the window.
scenes.narration: Same age, different history. So age alone may not set the window. Hearing a tutor seems to help close it.

scenes.tts: But missing input delays the closing; it does not abolish it. These birds eventually crystallize a song of their own.
scenes.visual: The isolate's timeline stretches farther, then ends at its own crystallized song. Label: delayed, not abolished.
scenes.narration: But missing input delays the closing; it does not abolish it. These birds eventually crystallize a song of their own.

scenes.tts: So experience seems to help set the window. Now, which part of the brain does the learning?
scenes.visual: A bird brain outline appears, with song nuclei as empty circles.
scenes.narration: So experience seems to help set the window. Now, which part of the brain does the learning?

scenes.tts: The motor pathway runs from H V C to R A, to brainstem neurons that drive the vocal organ.
scenes.caption: The motor pathway runs from HVC to RA, to brainstem neurons that drive the vocal organ.
scenes.visual: The motor pathway draws: HVC to RA to brainstem motor neurons to the syrinx. Label: motor pathway.
scenes.narration: The motor pathway runs from HVC to RA, to brainstem neurons that drive the vocal organ.

scenes.tts: A second loop leaves H V C. It runs through area X and the thalamus to L-man, then back to R A.
scenes.caption: A second loop leaves HVC. It runs through area X and the thalamus to LMAN, then back to RA.
scenes.visual: The anterior forebrain loop lights up: HVC to area X to thalamus to LMAN and back to RA. Label: anterior forebrain pathway.
scenes.narration: A second loop leaves HVC. It runs through area X and the thalamus to LMAN, then back to RA.

scenes.tts: L-man lesions disrupted song development in young finches, but left stable adult song intact. This loop matters while song is learned.
scenes.caption: LMAN lesions disrupted song development in young finches, but left stable adult song intact. This loop matters while song is learned.
scenes.visual: Two panels: a juvenile with an LMAN lesion and a disordered developing song; an adult with an LMAN lesion and an intact song. Credit: Bottjer, Miesner and Arnold, 1984.
scenes.narration: LMAN lesions disrupted song development in young finches, but left stable adult song intact. This loop matters while song is learned.

scenes.tts: In this loop, NMDA receptors were a natural suspect. Glutamate and a helper molecule, a co-agonist, activate them.
scenes.visual: An NMDA receptor diagram with two binding sites lighting up: glutamate; glycine or D-serine. Label: these open the channel.
scenes.narration: In this loop, NMDA receptors were a natural suspect. Glutamate and a helper molecule, a co-agonist, activate them.

scenes.tts: But at normal magnesium levels, magnesium plugs the pore until the receiving cell is depolarized.
scenes.visual: A magnesium ion sits in the open pore near rest. The receiving cell depolarizes, the magnesium is driven out, and ions flow. Label: depolarization relieves the magnesium block.
scenes.narration: But at normal magnesium levels, magnesium plugs the pore until the receiving cell is depolarized.

scenes.tts: So current flows mainly when glutamate is released and the receiving cell is depolarized at about the same time. In many brain regions, that strengthens the active synapse.
scenes.visual: Glutamate arrives just as the receiving cell is depolarized; the receptor between them lights up and the synapse thickens. Label: coincidence detector.
scenes.narration: So current flows mainly when glutamate is released and the receiving cell is depolarized at about the same time. In many brain regions, that strengthens the active synapse.

scenes.tts: Mark Basham and colleagues infused a blocker, A P five.
scenes.caption: Mark Basham and colleagues infused a blocker, AP5.
scenes.visual: Credit card: Basham, Nordeen and Nordeen, 1996. A cannula delivers AP5 into a finch brain.
scenes.narration: Mark Basham and colleagues infused a blocker, AP5.

scenes.tts: Predict. Which birds copy poorly? Blocker in the anterior forebrain before tutoring, there on other days only, or in the cerebellum?
scenes.visual: A three-row control table: AP5 in the anterior forebrain before each of ten tutoring sessions; AP5 there on non-tutoring days only; AP5 into the cerebellum. Column: copied? with question marks.
scenes.narration: Predict. Which birds copy poorly? Blocker in the anterior forebrain before tutoring, there on other days only, or in the cerebellum?

scenes.tts: Only the first group copied less.
scenes.visual: Row 1 fills: copied significantly less. Rows 2 and 3 fill: copied normally.
scenes.narration: Only the first group copied less.

scenes.tts: Birds given A P five on other days copied normally. That counts against lost practice alone, though birds could catch up between infusions.
scenes.visual: Row 2, weakens: a deficit from lost practice alone (not fully excluded).
scenes.narration: Birds given AP5 on other days copied normally. That counts against lost practice alone, though birds could catch up between infusions.
scenes.caption: Birds given AP5 on other days copied normally. That counts against lost practice alone, though birds could catch up between infusions.

scenes.tts: Cerebellum infusions left learning normal. And the A P five treated birds could still tell finch song from canary song, so they were not simply deaf to it.
scenes.visual: Row 3, argues against column: an effect of the drug wherever it is infused. A side panel: zebra finch song versus canary song, told apart. Label: not simply deaf.
scenes.narration: Cerebellum infusions left learning normal. And the A P five treated birds could still tell finch song from canary song, so they were not simply deaf to it.

scenes.tts: So NMDA receptors there are needed while the song is memorized. Where the memory is stored is not shown.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: NMDA receptors in the anterior forebrain are needed during tutoring. Below, smaller: where the memory is stored, not shown.
scenes.narration: So NMDA receptors there are needed while the song is memorized. Where the memory is stored is not shown.
